tasks.title: Run 114 pdf_android unit tests on Linux host & CI
tasks.desc:
Make `crates/pdf_android` pure unit tests execute on Linux host and in CI instead of only compiling.
- [ ] Gate Android-only deps (`android-activity`, `ndk`, `jni`, `android_logger`) under `cfg(target_os = "android")` without adding a new crate

notes.text: Approved. (relayed from chat by the agent)

Plan: see what breaks when building pdf_android tests on Linux, move the Android-only libraries behind an Android-only switch with the smallest code changes, get all 114 tests passing on Linux, then add a test step to CI.

All 114 pdf_android tests pass on Linux (cargo test -p pdf_android --lib), no warnings, host clippy clean. Android build not checked locally (NDK download blocked in this container); relying on the CI android job (check + clippy aarch64) for commit a9ac0a4.

The 114 pdf_android unit tests now run and pass on Linux and in CI (new CI step "test pdf_android (host)"), instead of only compiling for Android.
- Try it: `cargo test -p pdf_android --lib` (needs a placeholder crates/pdf_android/google_key.txt, as CI already does)
- Android build unchanged: CI run 200 is green, including check + clippy -D warnings for aarch64
- How: Android-only crates are behind cfg(target_os = "android"); on Linux, small do-nothing stand-ins in src/host/ and src/jni/host.rs take their place. The event loop and GPU library linking are Android-only.
- Bonus fix: the GPU code typed C strings as u8, which was only correct on ARM; now c_char (no change on the tablet).
- To check: you are fine with stand-in files living in the crate (they are never compiled into the app).
Accepted in chat. (relayed from chat by the agent)

tasks.title: Unify atomic file writes in persist.rs & export.rs
tasks.desc:
Prevent corrupted library or reader state on crash/power loss by replacing raw `fs::write` calls with temp-file + rename.
- [ ] One minimal atomic write helper used by all 6 writes in `persist.rs` and `export_markdown_to_file` in `export.rs`
- [ ] Unit tests confirm no leftover temp files and prior file stays intact on write failure

notes.text: Approved in chat (all cards). Tablet cards: agents do code + tests, human verifies on device. UI-02: human allowed merging to main and merging/closing the Dependabot PRs. (relayed from chat by the agent)
Plan: a dedicated agent works on it test-first in its own worktree; the orchestrator reviews the TDD history (failing test committed before the fix), merges into the session branch and checks CI.

Saving the library, reading progress, tool settings, recents, papers and Discover state, and the Markdown export, can no longer leave a half-written or empty file after a crash or power loss.
- Every one of those 7 writes now goes through one helper (pdf_core::write_atomic): write a hidden temp file next to the target, sync it to disk, then swap it in. On any error the old file stays as it was and the temp file is removed.
- TDD verified by the orchestrator: the tests committed first fail against a stub that writes in place (4 failures, incl. one covering all 6 saves), and pass after the change. 129 pdf_android tests pass after merging; workspace clippy and fmt clean.
- Follow-up idea, not done: two older JSON-only helpers in folder_sync could reuse it; one leaves its temp file behind on failure.
- On the tablet: nothing visible should change; opening the app with your existing library and progress is the check.

Correction: right after the merge, one pdf_android test run showed 1 failure (128/129) while 5 agents were compiling; the push went out before I caught it. 100+ reruns since (alone, 12 in parallel, CPU-saturated) all pass 129/129. Suspect: the pre-existing timing assertion (< 600 ms) in folder_sync's annotation-worker test, which this card does not touch. Proposed TD-03 to fix it.

tasks.title: Fix 2 flaky folder_sync timing tests (CI fails at random)
tasks.desc:
CI now fails at random: since TD-01 started running pdf_android tests in CI, two pre-existing folder_sync tests fail on slow runners (CI runs 204 and 206; the same commits pass on rerun):
- `annotation_worker_serializes_snapshots_to_sqlite_before_export_delay`: requires a background SQLite save within 600 ms
- `failed_export_does_not_block_local_sqlite_save_for_another_pdf`
Neither was changed today; they rely on wall-clock time.
Done means: both tests still prove what they prove now (save happens before the export delay; a failed export doesn't block other saves), but without timing bounds a slow machine can break, and the pdf_android suite passes repeatedly under heavy load.

notes.text: Added CI evidence: 2 failing tests, runs 204 and 206

Now failing in most CI runs (210, 211, 212). Worth checking while fixing: whether the worker's export path got slower (e.g. CO-01's fsync in export_markdown_to_file), since both tests assert the local save does not wait behind export.
